newsitem.title: UK: UK's BAe buys into Lagadere's bid for Thomson.
newsitem.headline: UK's BAe buys into Lagadere's bid for Thomson.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc joined the battle for takeover of the French defence electronics group Thomson-CSF on Wednesday, with the announcement that it was putting up 300 million pounds ($490.5 million) towards the bid being made by its French partner Lagadere.
BAe said it has extended its backing for Lagardere's bid with a view to taking joint control of Thomson's naval systems business if Lagadere wins.
Under the privatisation plan, Lagardere and rival suitor Alcatel Alsthom Cie Generale d'Electricite' submitted their final bids for Thomson earlier today.
It was announced last year that BAe would be backing Lagadere's bid with a view to absorbing Thomson's missile business into Matra BAe Dynamics (MBD), its own missile joint venture with Lagardere.

But BAe said on Wednesday that it has now also agreed with Lagadere that MBD would take over the BAe and Thomson naval businesses if Lagardere's bid is successful, with BAe putting up 300 million pounds.

"The agreement between British Aerospace and Lagardere has been widened to extend the business activities of MBD to include British Aerospace's naval systems businesses and the naval systems activities of Thomson-CSF if Lagardere succeeds in its bid for Thomson-CSF," BAe said in a statement.

"British Aerospace has agreed to provide finance in support of Lagardre's bid for Thomson-CSF of up to 2.7 billion francs ($464.2 million). This is to be effected by making a loan of 1.2 billion francs to MBD, paying a commercial rate of interest, together with an investment of 1.5 billion francs in the exchangeable bond announced by Lagardere today," the statement said.
Lagardere announced earlier that it would issue a special five-billion franc bond convertible into Thomson-CSF shares to help fund the deal, along with its own cash and credit lines.

The French government has banned foreign firms from making their own bids for Thomson, on the grounds of national security interests, but has left open the possibility for the winning bidder to form joint ventures with foreign firms.

Earlier today, Britain's GEC said it had signed memoranda of understanding with both Lagardere and Alcatel that whichever wins would enter talks with the British group about combining Thomson businesses with its own GEC-Marconi defence electronics to warships division.
The French government's sale of its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF is seen as opening the way for the long-awaited consolidation of the European defence industry.

Analysts said last year that in addition to missiles they suspected BAe would also have its eye on Thomson-CSF's naval business, as a way of extending its capabilities as a prime contractor to naval warfare. Thomson is prime contractor for Lafayette frigates.
-- Greg Mahlich, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717 ($ = 0.611 British Pounds) ($ = 5.817 French Francs)
